Tick-level martingale recovery loops and potential margin-dependent sizing make this unsuitable for naive Python conversion.

other_exits: Martingale recovery: positions are not closed by stop loss in traditional sense; the EA uses a martingale multiplier to increase lot size after a loss, aiming to recover losses on the next winning trade.

position_sizing.conditional_logic: On loss, multiply lot size by multiplier (default 2.0). On win, reset to initial_lots.

custom_logic_notes: Martingale lot sizing: after a losing trade, the next trade lot size is multiplied by a configurable multiplier (typically 2x). After a winning trade, lot size resets to the base value. RSI overbought/oversold levels (70/30) serve as entry signals. The combination of RSI mean-reversion with martingale position sizing creates exponential risk exposure during losing streaks, making this EA highly dependent on margin availability and broker position limits.
python_conversion_notes: Martingale position sizing must be carefully replicated with proper margin checking. The lot multiplication after losses requires trade history tracking to detect win/loss sequences. RSI signal generation is straightforward using ta-lib or pandas-ta, but the martingale recovery logic with margin-dependent lot sizing and potential account blow-up scenarios requires Monte Carlo simulation for proper backtesting. Fixed SL/TP values likely need _Digits/_Point adjustment (multiply by 10 for 5-digit brokers). Tick data recommended due to on_tick execution and martingale sensitivity to fill prices.
